pr_title: RFC: API Change: usb: Make users call usb_enable. Provide global status callback.
pr_body:
This PR is for resolving point 1 from #13403
Closes #21419
pr_comments: @carlescufi @emob-nordic @finikorg After reviewing this and #20011 I think we should not introduce USB_DEVICE_AUTO_ENABLE and drop 7bc65fabccc57cb8d4235ac9a8d2a604b33ba856

> Note that once there's an option to add a callback after USB has been initialized we need a way to ensure that the application tracks the state correctly: either by returning the state, or by having the callback invoked with an initial state when it's registered.

@pabigot This callback is used for notification only. The stack does not have to care about what application does with that. btw, I think a message queue or mailbox would be a better solution, but needs more work.

@pabigot 
>As implemented the new USB device state enumeration is not used. It should be removed, or the DC states mapped to device states. This is the blocker, the rest is commentary.

The usb_device_state was prepared for users so they will not create their own enum for this. Nothing more.

I understand that ideally user_state_callback should use [usb_device_state](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/20375/files#diff-0a5e6a18914d2e2bf1bf9595e8ab483eR105) as an input parameter but:
- from what I checked it would only apply for nordic (some vendors forward only 2 statuses which is weird but it is done like this and its not my intention here to correct drivers).

Ideally We would have field device_state in usb_dev singleton and then based on **status** callback we could change the **state** internally in the device and then call  proper user callback to keep him informed about the **state**.

Just to clarify the view of this PR. What basically happens here is:
- throw away the hid_ops.status_cb and makes it global per device, not per class as this should never be class specific.

> which is a little odd. It's not obvious how those map to device states (which should be extended to include a "DISCONNECTED" state, if that enum is going to be used).

usb_state will not include DISCONNECTED state as its not consistent with the spec and for this I would not agree with You.

> Just to clarify the view of this PR. What basically happens here is:
> 
> * throw away the hid_ops.status_cb and makes it global per device, not per class as this should never be class specific.

That's a good goal.

> The usb_device_state was prepared for users so they will not create their own enum for this. Nothing more.
> usb_state will not include DISCONNECTED state as its not consistent with the spec

I don't see the value in providing this enum if it's not going to be handled by the driver.  To this point AFAIK no classes have had any use for these states.  Even if they did, your point that some vendor implementations don't provide enough detail through DC states to distinguish them suggests they aren't generally useful.

Whatever receives the state changes will still have to interpret the DC states provided in the callback and translate them into whatever states are important.  For me that's "connected/working" and "disconnected/not working".  I do not care about the finer-grained states in `enum usb_state`.

I need a compelling reason why `enum usb_state` should remain, or fairly consistent agreement from the "real" USB maintainers that it should be here even if it's not used, before I withdraw the NAK.
@pabigot, @jfischer-phytec-iot  I've updated suggested changes. Please check it once again and approve if it's fine.
As per the API meeting, @emob-nordic please bring back the Kconfig option in #20011 to conditionally disable the auto-powerup of the USB stack into this PR.

> As per the API meeting, @emob-nordic please bring back the Kconfig option in #20011 to conditionally disable the auto-powerup of the USB stack into this PR.

Disagree, that is not the problem, the cb argument breaks the API.
But there is more to discuss, this PR breaks also netusb support.

> > As per the API meeting, @emob-nordic please bring back the Kconfig option in #20011 to conditionally disable the auto-powerup of the USB stack into this PR.
> 
> Disagree, that is not the problem, the cb argument breaks the API.
> But there is more to discuss, this PR breaks also netusb support.

I will leave this discussion for USB sync meeting today.

@emob-nordic  please follow [the new procedure](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/development_process/api_lifecycle.html#introducing-incompatible-changes) and let's not introduce the Kconfig option, taking the opportunity to clean this up since we are introducing incompatible changes anyway.

> Seems like there should be some usage documentation changes for this (other than in the doxygen comments and release notes)...

What would You suggest? I was following the [process](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/development_process/api_lifecycle.html#introducing-incompatible-changes) and hoped this is sufficient.

> Seems like there should be some usage documentation changes for this (other than in the doxygen comments and release notes)...

I proposed a rewritten section in the release notes. Beyond this and the doxygen changes, there is currently no documentation which explains to the users the USB subsystem usage, so I do not think any further changes are necessary until we add more documentation @dbkinder.
The change follows standard procedure as pointed out by @emob-nordic

issue_context.title: RFC: API Change: usb: Make users call usb_enable. Provide global status callback.
issue_context.body:
## Introduction

* Users should have a possibility to call usb_enable when they wants to (like its done for bluetooth). Currently usb is auto enabled on system boot up which may lead to errors (explained later).

* USB status codes should refer to USB device as a whole not to a particular class as it is done now (HID). 

### Problem description

* It is possible that usb is enabled before the class specific init function is called. If that happen usb hardware may start to produce events that will be dropped because class is not initialized yet.

* Until now users were able to view the internal USB driver status codes only by using HID class. In fact usb status is global per a device not per function/class.

### Proposed change

Make users responsible for calling usb_enable and decide whenever hardware should start to work.

Provide global status callback which will indicate the status of USB.

## Detailed 

To solve above problems I propose:
Delete usb_enable() from [usb_device_init()](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/subsys/usb/usb_device.c#L1636) which is called on system boot up.

Add a callback parameter to usb_enable(). If user wants to monitor the status of USB he could use this callback.

### Proposed change (Detailed)

Please look to #20375 PR.

### Dependencies

Users that use USB will have to update their applications and call usb_enable() by themselves as it will be removed from system boot up initialization.
comments: Not sure if this is the case but if usb device can be seen as service requested and released asynchronously by multiple clients (classes) then you might want to keep your eye on `onoff_service` PR (#21090) which attempts to standardize such case.

review_comments: `if (usb_enable(status_cb))`?

Personal opinion: yeah, it could be[*], but that would make it slightly more inconvenient to add diagnostics to display exactly why it failed when debugging or maintaining.

[*] well, actually this:

```
if (usb_enable(status_cb) != 0) {
```

since we're courting MISRA these days and treating `int` values as booleans is not acceptable.

To be consistent with the documented behavior of `usb_enable()` this should be added, in case some of the intermediate functions returned a positive value:

    ret = 0;
To be honest I dont get it. if failure, then return success?

API documented behavior for `usb_enable()` is  _"0 on success, negative errno code on fail."_, so it is undefined for (ret > 0) :-)

But as we are here, should we cleanup and change this` if (ret < 0) `to `if (ret)`?
- `static int usb_vbus_set(bool on);` returns 0 on success, negative errno code on fail
- `int usb_dc_attach(void); `returns 0 on success, negative errno code on fail
- `int usb_dc_ep_configure(const struct usb_dc_ep_cfg_data * const cfg);` returns 0 on success, negative errno code on fail
- `int usb_dc_ep_set_callback(const u8_t ep, const usb_dc_ep_callback cb);` returns 0 on success, negative errno code on fail
- `static int composite_setup_ep_cb(void); `returns 0 on success, negative errno code on fail
- `int usb_dc_ep_enable(const u8_t ep);` returns 0 on success, negative errno code on fail

> API documented behavior for `usb_enable()` is _"0 on success, negative errno code on fail."_, so it is undefined for (ret > 0) :-)

Exactly.  Failing to describe the complete value range of input and output parameters is pervasive problem in Zephyr.

> But as we are here, should we cleanup and change this`if (ret < 0)`to `if (ret)`?

Changing to `if (ret != 0)` would be acceptable as it satisfies the return guarantee--as long as none of those functions return positive.  Making a maintainer search for the documented (and implemented) behavior of all those subordinate functions to confirm the API  is not reasonable IMO, hence the change request.
@emob-nordic Do you agree with "Changing to if (ret != 0) would be acceptable" ?
Yes, now I get the point. I will update it in a minute.
The above check for `usb_dev.enabled` must be moved after the mutex is acquired, or two threads could pass that check then sequentially both initialize the controller.
Good point. I missed this case.
Guess it was my fault too.
`if (usb_enable(status_cb))`?
`if (usb_enable(status_cb))`?
blank space after `}`
So to use this callback we shall call usb_enable(cb) always?
Yes. If callback is needed then USB_DEVICE_AUTO_ENABLE=n and call usb_enable(cb) in the app.

Here's one where I'm not responsible for this, so I won't block, but: This is unilaterally changing existing behavior of a subsystem, requiring code to change so the application continues to work.  There's no documentation of this change.  At a minimum it should be part of a release note on changed API.  Somebody should figure out how to make that work.

The story behind this change starts from Nordic application team. There was a problem with missed status_callbacks in [hid_ops.status_cb](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/include/usb/class/usb_hid.h#L85) Two issues here:
1) status callback should never been associated with class.
2) usb_enable() calls usb_dc_attach() and by that call interrupts are enabled. Because it happens on SYS_INIT and user app is registering HID callbacks by itself (after system is woken up), it is possible to get the interrupt from usbd and in particular miss some statuses in the APP.

By this change we let the user to control usb_enable function and by that avoid those misses.

By this change you **require** the user to control `usb_enable()`, causing all existing USB applications to break until they are modified to enable USB explicitly, just as you've done for the examples.  Or am I wrong about that?

I understand the reason for the change but a comment here in the PR doesn't help the maintainers of existing code figure out why their applications no longer work.
@pabigot I will update documentation in commit in which I am changing from _auto enable_ to _enable by user_ as well as PR message. Would this be sufficient?

@pabigot you raise a good point but here are the circumstances around this that I'd like to point out to warrant an exception in this particular case:

- The current behavior was inconsistent with other protocol stacks in Zephyr, and in particular with Bluetooth, that requires a `bt_enable()` call from the sample that controls the moment at which we power on the hardware.
- The `usb_enable()` function was almost useless in the form that existed until this PR, and we are now giving it a purpose.
- I agree we need to document this behavior in two places: The doxygen for `usb_enable()` itself and the release notes (2.2 release notes at this point).
- We will merge this change right in the beginning of the 2.2 release cycle, which give ample time to users that follow master to adapt.
- Deprecating the current behavior would not benefit users in any meaningful way, because of the current inconsistent and incorrect behavior of this `usb_enable()` API.
- For users of standard provided classes that expose an API, eg. HID there was a race condition with the current master behavior of auto-enabling the USB stack: the USB stack was enabled before the user had a chance to register a HID device, meaning that events could be lost in between.
